title: John Baptist de La Salle (7 April)
hookLine: a wealthy canon who gave up his comfort to start free schools for poor boys

lines: A CANON WITH AN ENVIABLE LIFE.
cards: A young priest in Reims has the kind of life people envy. A rich family, a fine house, a seat as a canon at the cathedral, good dinners, good books.
Then he agrees to help a man who wants to open schools for poor boys, the kind who spend their days in the street. Just a bit of advice. Then he finds the teachers a place to stay.
Then, because they're struggling, he invites them to eat at his own table. His family is appalled. These men are rough, untrained, poorly paid.
He keeps saying yes, one small step at a time.

teach.h: ONE SMALL STEP AT A TIME.
teach.b: John Baptist de La Salle later said that if he had known where those first steps would lead, he might never have taken them. But he took them. He brought the teachers into his own house to live.

teach.h: HE GAVE UP HIS POST AND HIS FORTUNE.
teach.b: Then he gave up his post at the cathedral. Then, tradition says, during a time of hunger, he gave away his family fortune to the poor, so he would stand where his teachers stood, with nothing to fall back on.
Out of that household came a community: the Brothers of the Christian Schools. They weren't priests.

teach.h: BROTHERS WHO TAUGHT POOR CHILDREN FREE.
teach.b: They were laymen who made vows and gave their lives to one thing, teaching poor children, for free. La Salle changed how the teaching was done. Lessons in the children's own language, French, instead of Latin.

Children grouped by what they knew and taught together, not one at a time while the rest waited. And training for the teachers, so a teacher wasn't just whoever could be found, but someone formed for the work.

teach.h: A NEW WAY TO RUN A CLASSROOM.
teach.b: He also wrote for his brothers about the inner side of teaching: that a classroom is a place where God is present, and that they should recognize Jesus in the poor children in front of them.
The prophet Daniel has a line about teachers, in the Douay-Rheims: "they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity." The Church later named La Salle patron of teachers.
It began with a few hungry teachers at his table.

how: Catholics keep John Baptist de La Salle's memorial on 7 April; the De La Salle Brothers and their schools honor him as their founder.

games.q: you're a wealthy canon. the struggling teachers you've been helping need a home, and your family is appalled. what do you do?
o: give them money, and keep your distance.
take them into your own house.
games.why: he brought them into his own house, then gave up his post and his fortune, and the Brothers were born.

practice: Bring to mind one teacher who changed something for you: a schoolteacher, a coach, a grandparent at a kitchen table, a boss who took time to show you how.
Remember one specific thing they did, a sentence, a second chance, a moment they didn't give up on you. If you pray, thank God for them; if you don't, just let the gratitude be real.
